answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive in time, not just tokens: a new account posts a bond that must season untouched across several epochs before it can earn or vote, like an orchard that bears nothing in its first years. Planting a thousand fake rows means locking a thousand bonds and waiting out every season for each one, while a river of cross-checks links wallets that move together, and one proven fake burns the whole cluster's stake. An honest agent crosses that ridge once; an attacker pays it per fake, in capital and in months, before earning anything.
